title: Fix: autoscaler priority routing causing burst token miscount and incorrect utilization reporting
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We observed two related issues in Dedicated autoscaler operation under mixed-priority traffic: 1) the priority router was delegating burst tokens to lower-priority pools when higher-priority pools had transient capacity, which led to incorrect token accounting and occasional over-bursting on lower tiers; 2) utilization reporting for dedicated fleets double-counted in-flight KV cache evictions under certain retry/error conditions, causing utilization metrics to be inflated by ~5-12% in dashboards. Both issues impact throughput guarantees and billing/alerting accuracy. This PR fixes the root causes, adds targeted unit and integration tests, and updates metrics to be robust to transient error paths. Summary of changes: - Fix priority token accounting: autoscaler/tokenbucket.go: ensure tokens reserved for a priority tier are not reassigned until the reservation window expires; add deterministic arbitration when multiple priorities contend. - Priority routing guard: router/priority_router.go: add a fast-path check to avoid delegating bursts if upstream capacity is likely to be re-used by the original owner (heuristic based on recent reclaimable tokens and lease timestamps). - Utilization reporting correction: metrics/util_reporter.go: remove double-counting of eviction-related inflight counters and add explicit tags for eviction vs. active-serving tokens. - Tests and e2e: tests/autoscaler/* and e2e/dedicated_autoscale_priority.yaml: new unit tests for tokenbucket concurrency and an e2e scenario reproducing the original issue. - Observability: dashboards/queries: update the dedicated-fleet utilization query to use the corrected eviction tags. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced issue locally and with canary traffic - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration/e2e added - [x] Updated dashboard query and added note to changelog - [x] CI green after rerun Note: The description below includes implementation rationale and trade-offs. Implementation details: - Token reservation window: introduced a per-reservation TTL (configurable; default 5s) to avoid immediate reallocation across priority boundaries. This prevents pathological thrash when workloads oscillate between priorities. - Deterministic arbitration: when two priorities request the same tokens, we now prefer the higher SLA tier; ties broken by earliest-request timestamp. This logic is encapsulated in tokenbucket.ReserveWithPriority. - Metrics tagging: previously util_reporter aggregated "inflight_evictions" into the generic "inflight" metric. That aggregation could happen twice when eviction cleanup triggered a retry path that also incremented the inflight counter. We split the counters and updated the reporting query to sum only active-serving counters for SLA and billing calculations. Performance impact: microbenchmarks show negligible added latency in the hot path (~0.05ms median per-request) due to the added fast-path check; throughput unchanged within noise. Backwards compatibility: config default preserves previous behavior except for the bug fix; operators can tune reservation_ttl via Dedicated config. Related: ENG-2345 (priority autoscaler correctness), ENG-2370 (utilization reporting follow-up), SUP-987 (customer support case that escalated this bug).

release_notes:
- Fix: Prevent token misallocation across priority tiers in Dedicated autoscaler (improves burst isolation and throughput guarantees)
- Fix: Correct dedicated fleet utilization reporting to avoid double-counting eviction-related inflight counters
- Tests: Added unit and e2e coverage for priority-based bursting
Operators: reservation_ttl default is 5s; configurable via dedicated config.
